name: Healthy / Normal Operation
description: Vibration frequency and amplitude are within the normal range expected for smoothly running rotating equipment.
recommendation: No action needed. Continue routine monitoring.

name: Imbalance (e.g. bent fan blade, uneven load)
description: A single dominant low-frequency peak with large amplitude often indicates rotating imbalance, such as a bent blade, debris buildup, or uneven mass distribution.
recommendation: Inspect for visible debris, bent blades, or loose attachments. Consider rebalancing.

name: Mechanical Looseness
description: Irregular, less predictable vibration in this range can point to loose mounting bolts, worn brackets, or a loose housing.
recommendation: Check and tighten mounting hardware. Inspect brackets and housing for wear.

name: Bearing Wear (early stage)
description: High-frequency vibration at relatively low amplitude is a classic early sign of bearing wear, before it becomes audible or severe.
recommendation: Schedule a bearing inspection within the next few weeks. Monitor amplitude trend closely.

name: Bearing Wear (advanced)
description: High-frequency vibration combined with high amplitude suggests significantly worn or damaged bearings.
recommendation: Recommend near-term inspection and likely bearing replacement to avoid failure.

name: Motor Electrical Fault (e.g. winding issue)
description: A sharp peak very close to twice the electrical line frequency (around 100 Hz for 50Hz mains) can indicate an electrical fault such as winding or rotor bar issues, rather than a purely mechanical one.
recommendation: Have an electrician check motor windings and power supply quality.
